title: The Eagle's EGGs
caption: The Eagle Nebula in infrared, imaged by the Very Large Telescope
celestial: Eagle Nebula, M 16, Messier 16, NGC 6611 · constellation Serpens Cauda

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: At the center of this infrared view of the Eagle Nebula, also called Messier 16, stand the famous Pillars of Creation, joined by several other pillars in the same star-forming region. Stars crowd the whole frame. At upper right, a cluster of bright blue stars marks NGC 6611, whose massive, hot stars light up the pillars.

The colors tell the stars apart. Blue ones belong either to the young cluster NGC 6611 or are foreground stars along our line of sight. Most stars look fainter and yellower. They are ordinary stars far behind M16, seen through the clouds from which the cluster formed. A few very red stars are either very young and still wrapped in gas and dust, or brighter background stars shining through it.
The picture is a mosaic of 144 images from the ISAAC instrument on the VLT's Antu telescope, sensitive enough to detect young stars of all masses.

understand.summary: This near-infrared image comes from the ISAAC instrument on ESO's Very Large Telescope. The Js band (1.24 μm) is shown as blue, H (1.65 μm) as green and Ks (2.16 μm) as red.
filters: 1.24 μm · Infrared J (Very Large Telescope ISAAC)

understand.eye: Near-infrared light is invisible to the eye, and it passes through dust more easily than visible light, revealing stars inside and behind the clouds.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.

explore: The Eagle Nebula lies in the constellation of Serpens, about 6,500 light-years away. The mosaic covers roughly 17 x 17 light-years, and the image sharpness reaches about 0.35 arcseconds. To bring out faint gas, the brightness of each band was compressed before the colors were combined.
alt: An infrared view of a nebula with pillars at the center, a cluster of blue stars at upper right and a dense field of yellow and red stars.
